headings: Our Brands and Intellectual Property Rights
paragraphs: When used in this report, the terms "we," "us," "our," "PepsiCo" and the "Company" mean PepsiCo, Inc. and its consolidated subsidiaries, collectively. Certain terms used in this Annual Report on Form 10-K are defined in the Glossary included in Item 7. of this report.

We were incorporated in Delaware in 1919 and reincorporated in North Carolina in 1986. We are a leading global beverage and convenient food company with a complementary portfolio of brands, including Lay's, Doritos, Cheetos, Gatorade, Pepsi-Cola, Mountain Dew, Quaker and SodaStream. Through our operations, authorized bottlers, contract manufacturers and other third parties, we make, market, distribute and sell a wide variety of beverages and convenient foods, serving customers and consumers in more than 200 countries and territories.
We are organized into six reportable segments, as follows:
1)PepsiCo Foods North America (PFNA), which includes all of our convenient food businesses in the United States and Canada;
2)PepsiCo Beverages North America (PBNA), which includes all of our beverage businesses in the United States and Canada;
3)International Beverages Franchise (IB Franchise), which includes our international franchise beverage businesses, as well as our SodaStream business;
4)Europe, Middle East and Africa (EMEA), which includes our convenient food businesses and our beverage businesses with company-owned bottlers in Europe, the Middle East and Africa;
5)Latin America Foods (LatAm Foods), which includes all of our convenient food businesses in Latin America; and
6)Asia Pacific Foods, which consists of our convenient food businesses in Asia Pacific, including China, Australia and New Zealand, as well as India.

Either independently or in conjunction with third parties, PFNA makes, markets, distributes and sells convenient foods, which include cereals, chips, dips, granola bars, oatmeal, pasta, rice and syrups and mixes under various brands including Cheetos, Doritos, Fritos, Lay's, Pearl Milling Company, Quaker, Ruffles and Tostitos. PFNA's products are sold to independent distributors and retailers. In December 2024, we acquired the Strauss Group's 50% ownership in Sabra Dipping Company, LLC (Sabra) and Sabra became a wholly-owned subsidiary. Sabra makes, markets, distributes and sells Sabra refrigerated dips and spreads.

Either independently or in conjunction with third parties, PBNA makes, markets and sells beverage concentrates, fountain syrups and finished goods under various beverage brands including Aquafina, Bubly, Diet Mountain Dew, Diet Pepsi, Gatorade, Gatorade Zero, Mountain Dew, Mountain Dew Baja Blast, Pepsi, Pepsi Wild Cherry, Pepsi Zero Sugar and Propel. PBNA operates its own bottling plants and distribution facilities and sells branded finished goods directly to independent distributors and retailers. PBNA also sells concentrate and finished goods for our brands to authorized and independent bottlers, who in turn sell our branded finished goods to independent distributors and retailers in certain markets. PBNA also, either independently or in conjunction with third parties, makes, markets, distributes and sells ready-to-drink tea and coffee products through joint ventures with Unilever (under the Lipton brand name) and Starbucks, respectively. Further, PBNA manufactures and distributes certain brands licensed from Keurig Dr Pepper Inc., including Crush, Dr Pepper and Schweppes, and certain juice brands licensed from Dole Food Company, Inc. and Ocean Spray Cranberries, Inc. PBNA also distributes, in certain channels, brands owned by Celsius Holdings, Inc. (Celsius), including Celsius, Alani Nu and Rockstar. In the United States, PBNA acts as the exclusive distributor for small-format and foodservice customers with chilled direct-store-delivery (DSD) for the portfolio of brands owned by Tropicana Beverages Group (TBG).

IB Franchise makes, markets and sells beverage concentrates to authorized and independent bottlers under various beverage brands including 7UP, Aquafina, Gatorade, Mirinda, Mountain Dew, Pepsi, Pepsi Black, Pepsi Zero Sugar, and Sting Energy. IB Franchise also manufactures and distributes SodaStream sparkling water makers and related products. Further, IB Franchise, either independently or in conjunction with third parties, makes, markets, distributes and sells ready-to-drink tea products through an international joint venture with Unilever (under the Lipton brand name).

Either independently or in conjunction with third parties, EMEA makes, markets, distributes and sells a number of convenient food brands including Cheetos, Chipsy, Doritos, Lay's, Quaker, Sasko, Spekko, Walkers and White Star through consolidated businesses, as well as through noncontrolled affiliates. EMEA also, either independently or in conjunction with third parties, makes, markets, distributes and sells a number of beverage brands including 7UP, Adrenaline Rush, Aquafina, Lubimy, Mirinda, Pepsi and Pepsi Zero Sugar. EMEA operates its own bottling plants and distribution facilities and sells finished goods directly to independent distributors and retailers. Further, EMEA makes, markets, distributes and sells a number of dairy products including Agusha, Chudo and Domik v Derevne. EMEA also, either

independently or in conjunction with third parties, makes, markets, distributes and sells ready-to-drink tea products through an international joint venture with Unilever (under the Lipton brand name).

paragraphs: The following risks, some of which have occurred and any of which may occur in the future, can have a material adverse effect on our business or financial performance, which in turn can affect the price of our publicly traded securities. These are not the only risks we face. There may be other risks we are not currently aware of or that we currently deem not to be material but that may become material in the future.

Demand for our products depends in part on our ability to innovate and anticipate and effectively respond to shifts in consumer trends and preferences, including the types of products our consumers want and how they browse for, purchase and consume them. Consumer preferences continuously evolve due to a variety of factors, including: changes in consumer demographics, consumption patterns (including increased food purchased away-from-home), diet (whether due to changes in consumer behavior and eating habits, increasing use of weight-loss drugs, such as GLP-1 medications, or other factors) and channel preferences (including continued increases in the e-commerce and online-to-offline channels and use of artificial intelligence shopping agents that autonomously select products that may not be ours); pricing (including the effective impact of tariffs and taxes imposed on the manufacture, distribution or sale of certain of our products as a result of ingredients contained in such products); affordability pressures and changes in consumer spending patterns (including if consumers switch to private label or lower-priced product offerings); changes in funding for or restrictions on the inclusion of our products in benefit programs, such as the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) in the United States; product quality; product functionality (including products high in protein or fiber-enriched); concerns or perceptions regarding packaging and its environmental impact (such as single-use and other plastic packaging); concerns or perceptions regarding the processing, nutrition profile and health effects of, or location of origin of, ingredients or substances in our products or packaging, including due to public statements by government officials, increased litigation, changes in regulations, regulatory scrutiny or the results of third-party studies (whether or not scientifically valid); and concerns or perceptions regarding our workforce policies and initiatives. Concerns with any of the foregoing have affected and may continue to affect consumer behaviors and can lead consumers to reduce or publicly boycott the purchase or consumption of our products.

Pandemics, epidemics or other disease outbreaks and geopolitical events and tensions, wars and other military conflicts have also impacted and could continue to impact consumer preferences and demand for our products, including negative consumer sentiment toward non-local products. Consumer preferences are also influenced by perception of our brand image or the brand images of our products, the success of our advertising and marketing campaigns, our ability to engage with our consumers in the manner they prefer, including through the use of digital media or assets, and the perception of our use of social media and our response to political and social issues, geopolitical events and tensions, wars and other military conflicts or catastrophic events. These and other factors have reduced and could continue to reduce consumers' willingness to purchase certain of our products, including as a result of public boycotts. Any inability on our part to anticipate or react to changes in consumer preferences and trends, or make the right strategic investments to do so, including investments in artificial intelligence and data analytics to understand consumer trends, can lead to reduced demand for our products, lead to inventory write-offs or erode our competitive and financial position, thereby adversely affecting our business. In addition, our business operations, including our supply chain, are subject to disruption by geopolitical events and tensions, wars and other military conflicts, natural disasters, pandemics, epidemics or other events beyond
our control that could negatively impact product availability and decrease demand for our products if our crisis management plans do not effectively mitigate these issues.

Maintaining a positive reputation globally is important to our business. Our reputation or brand image has in the past been, and could in the future be, adversely impacted by a variety of factors, including: any failure by us, our business partners, or other actors in our supply chain to maintain high ethical, business and environmental, social and governance practices, including with respect to human rights, child labor, workforce policies and initiatives, workplace conditions and employee health and safety; any failure, or perceived failure, to achieve or make sufficient progress toward our environmental, social and governance goals, or any revisions of or negative perception toward such goals, including with respect to the nutrition profile of our products, packaging, water use, our impact on the environment and our workforce policies and initiatives; any difficulties executing our strategic initiatives; any failure to address health or other concerns about our products, products we distribute, certain brands licensed to and distributed to third parties (including alcoholic beverages), or particular ingredients or substances in our products, including concerns or perceptions regarding whether certain of our products are "ultra-processed," contain certain ingredients or substances or otherwise contribute to obesity and other health conditions or an increase in public health costs; our research and development efforts; any product quality or safety issues, including the recall of any of our products; any failure to comply with laws and regulations; consumer perception of our advertising campaigns, sponsorship arrangements, marketing programs, use of social media and our response to political and social issues, geopolitical events and tensions, wars and other military conflicts, or catastrophic events; or any failure to effectively respond to negative or inaccurate comments about us on social media or otherwise regarding any of the foregoing. Damage to our reputation or brand image has in the past and could in the future decrease demand for our products, thereby adversely affecting our business.

We have recalled, and could in the future recall, products due to product quality or safety issues, including actual or alleged mislabeling, misbranding, spoilage, undeclared allergens, adulteration or contamination. Joint ventures in which we have an interest have also recalled, and could in the future recall, products for the same or other reasons. These risks could be heightened in light of new or evolving regulations, changes to our portfolio (including increased use of functional or other ingredients), aging infrastructure, and increased pressure on our suppliers from supply chain disruptions. Product recalls have in the past and could in the future adversely affect our business by resulting in losses due to their cost, the destruction of product inventory, customer fines and returns or lost sales due to any unavailability of the product for a period of time. In addition, our manufacturing facilities and products have been and could continue to be subject to increased inspection by federal, state and local authorities. Product quality or safety issues identified by us or governmental authorities have in the past and could in the future also reduce consumer confidence and demand for our products, cause production and delivery disruptions, including as a result of temporary or permanent closure of manufacturing plants or facilities, result in increased costs (including payment of fines and/or judgments, cleaning and remediation costs and legal fees, and costs associated with alternative sources of production) and damage our reputation (or the reputation of joint ventures in which we have an interest), particularly as we or our joint ventures continue to expand into new categories, all of which can adversely affect our business. paragraphs: PepsiCo is a leading global beverage and convenient food company with a complementary portfolio of brands, including Lay's, Doritos, Cheetos, Gatorade, Pepsi-Cola, Mountain Dew, Quaker and SodaStream. Through our operations, authorized bottlers, contract manufacturers, and other third parties, we make, market, distribute, and sell a wide array of beverages and convenient foods, serving customers and consumers in more than 200 countries and territories.

As a global company with strong local connections, we faced many of the same challenges in 2025 as our consumers, customers, and competitors worldwide. These included ongoing supply chain disruptions; tariffs; persistent inflationary pressures; evolving consumer consumption patterns and preferences; an intensely competitive business environment, including the increased adoption of artificial intelligence technologies; the continued expansion of e-commerce in a rapidly changing retail landscape, including customers moving away from DSD systems; the need for further innovation and collaboration as we progress toward our ambitious packaging and other goals; ongoing macroeconomic and political volatility; and an increasingly complex regulatory environment.

In response to these challenges, we have continued to adapt and innovate, reinforcing our resilience and continued focus on growth. We are focused on improving our productivity, optimizing our operations and harnessing our scale and capabilities across our markets and further elevating the interests, occasions, and channels of consumers in our strategies to lead and shape the future of our categories. This is underpinned by our pep+ (PepsiCo Positive) transformation, now in its fifth year.

A Bold Ambition: Against this backdrop, we have a clear set of priorities: reigniting our North America business by combining operations where it makes the most sense and using the savings to support meaningful investments in our brands; increasing the size, presence and scale of our International business, with a focus on capturing growth in large and developing markets; and working to grow our away-from-home business by expanding our availability and extending into new occasions.

Laying the Groundwork: Since 2018, we have made significant investments in the business to adapt to the changing landscape. This includes increasing investments to strengthen our brands, from transforming our portfolio through innovation and acquisitions, to foundational investments in technology and artificial intelligence to position ourselves to be fit for the future, building a set of high impact commercial, operational, and digital capabilities; expanding and updating our manufacturing footprint to enable geographic growth and capture future demand; right-sizing and modernizing our warehousing and distribution capacity; and transforming our operating model to become more agile, efficient and responsive to the consumer.

Big Changes to Big Things: Guided by pep+, we continue to work to reshape our portfolio to fit today's world. That includes: reducing added sugar, sodium and saturated fat in core brands like Lay's and Gatorade; advancing efforts to remove artificial colors and flavors in brands like Lay's, Cheetos, and Doritos; adding new products with functional benefits, such as Pepsi Prebiotic Cola; and welcoming popular brands like Siete, Sabra and poppi.

We continued to expand our away-from-home business into new occasions. The successful Walking Taco platform is thriving in stadiums, arenas, and parks across the United States, while our "Food Deserves Pepsi" campaign and the "Pepsi Zero Sugar Taste Challenge" have driven higher brand awareness and contributed positively to our performance.

We are becoming a more deeply integrated, more productive organization. This has been one of our biggest priorities over the past year. Since we shifted our operating model at the start of 2025, we have worked hard to be more agile, simpler and more unified. From sharing global services, to streamlining processes, to launching our first new corporate brand identity in nearly 25 years, we are making One PepsiCo real. In North America, we are carefully evaluating an integrated model for our food and beverage supply chains, go-to-market, and commercial capabilities and intend to take a nuanced approach factoring in key components such as return on investment, scale and market share. Our Global Capability Centers now support multiple functions, enabling us to centralize information, reduce duplicative work, and share best practices across the organization.

We are building smarter systems with technologies like artificial intelligence to better serve our customers and consumers, so we can have the right products, at the right place, at the right price. Through our collaborations with cutting-edge technology providers, we are using artificial intelligence to reimagine our go-to-market model, enhance customer support, and empower sales teams to focus on strategic growth. This allows us to unify data, gain real-time inventory visibility, and provide faster, more responsive customer service.

We are becoming more resilient through pep+. pep+ remains central to our strategy, ensuring that we continue to create value for shareholders, customers and consumers, while doing what is right for communities and the planet. In 2025, we stepped up our efforts around key pillars like regenerative agriculture and water use efficiency, with the aim to make a positive impact in markets around the world.

paragraphs: 當本報告中使用 "we," "us," "our," "PepsiCo" 以及 "Company" 這些詞語時，係指 PepsiCo, Inc. 及其合併子公司， collectively。本年度報告 10-K 中使用之某些詞語係於本報告第 7 項所附之術語表中定義。

本公司於 1919 年在特拉華州設立，並於 1986 年轉移註冊至北卡羅來納州。本公司為全球知名的飲料與方便食品公司，擁有相互補充的品牌組合，包括 Lay's、Doritos、Cheetos、Gatorade、Pepsi-Cola、Mountain Dew、Quaker 及 SodaStream。透過本公司營運、授權灌裝商、契約製造商及其他第三方，我們製造、行銷、分銷及銷售多種飲料與方便食品，服務超過 200 個國家及地區的客戶與消費者。
本公司依下列六個應報告分部進行組織：
1)PepsiCo Foods North America (PFNA)，包含本公司於美國與加拿大所有方便食品業務；
2)PepsiCo Beverages North America (PBNA)，包含本公司於美國與加拿大所有飲料業務；
3)International Beverages Franchise (IB Franchise)，包含本公司國際特許飲料業務，以及 SodaStream 事業；
4)Europe, Middle East and Africa (EMEA)，包含本公司於歐洲、中東及非洲之方便食品業務，以及擁有公司自營灌裝商之飲料業務；
5)Latin America Foods (LatAm Foods)，包含本公司於拉丁美洲所有方便食品業務；
6)亞太地區食品，包含我們在亞太地區的便利食品業務，包括中國、澳洲與紐西蘭，以及印度。

PFNA 獨立或與第三方合作，製造、行銷、分銷與銷售便利食品，包含穀物、薯片、蘸醬、格蘭諾拉棒、燕麥粥、義大利麵、米與糖漿與混合調料，品牌包括 Cheetos、Doritos、Fritos、Lay's、Pearl Milling Company、Quaker、Ruffles 與 Tostitos。PFNA 的產品銷售給獨立的經銷商與零售商。2024 年 12 月，我們取得 Strauss Group 所持有的 Sabra Dipping Company, LLC（Sabra）50% 的股權，Sabra 成為本公司全資子公司。Sabra 製造、行銷、分銷與銷售 Sabra 冷藏蘸醬與醬料。

PBNA 獨立或與第三方合作，製造、行銷與銷售飲料濃縮液、現調糖漿與成品飲料，品牌包括 Aquafina、Bubly、Diet Mountain Dew、Diet Pepsi、Gatorade、Gatorade Zero、Mountain Dew、Mountain Dew Baja Blast、Pepsi、Pepsi Wild Cherry、Pepsi Zero Sugar 與 Propel。PBNA 自營製造廠與分銷設施，並直接銷售品牌成品飲料給獨立經銷商與零售商。PBNA 也銷售濃縮液與成品飲料給授權與獨立製造商，這些製造商再將本公司品牌成品飲料銷售給獨立經銷商與零售商。PBNA 也透過與 Unilever 的國際合資公司（Lipton 品牌名稱）與 Starbucks 的合作，製造、行銷、分銷與銷售即飲茶與咖啡產品。此外，PBNA 還製造與分銷來自 Keurig Dr Pepper Inc. 的授權品牌，包括 Crush、Dr Pepper 與 Schweppes，以及來自 Dole Food Company, Inc. 與 Ocean Spray Cranberries, Inc. 的果汁品牌。PBNA 也於特定通路分銷 Celsius Holdings, Inc.（Celsius）所擁有品牌，包括 Celsius、Alani Nu 與 Rockstar。在美國，PBNA 為 Tropicana Beverages Group（TBG）所擁有品牌的小容量與餐飲客戶提供獨家分銷服務，包含冷藏直送店內（DSD）的服務。

IB Franchise 獨立或與第三方合作，製造、行銷與銷售飲料濃縮液給授權與獨立製造商，品牌包括 7UP、Aquafina、Gatorade、Mirinda、Mountain Dew、Pepsi、Pepsi Black、Pepsi Zero Sugar 與 Sting Energy。IB Franchise 也製造與分銷 SodaStream 氣泡水製造機與相關產品。此外，IB Franchise 獨立或與第三方合作，透過與 Unilever 的國際合資公司（Lipton 品牌名稱）製造、行銷、分銷與銷售即飲茶產品。

EMEA 獨立或與第三方合作，製造、行銷、分銷與銷售多種便利食品品牌，包括 Cheetos、Chipsy、Doritos、Lay's、Quaker、Sasko、Spekko、Walkers 與 White Star，透過合併業務與非控制性附屬公司。EMEA 也獨立或與第三方合作，製造、行銷、分銷與銷售多種飲料品牌，包括 7UP、Adrenaline Rush、Aquafina、Lubimy、Mirinda、Pepsi 與 Pepsi Zero Sugar。EMEA 自營製造廠與分銷設施，並直接銷售成品飲料給獨立經銷商與零售商。此外，EMEA 也製造、行銷、分銷與銷售多種乳製品，包括 Agusha、Chudo 與 Domik v Derevne。EMEA 也
獨立或與第三方合作，透過與 Unilever 的國際合資公司（Lipton 品牌名稱）製造、行銷、分銷與銷售即飲茶產品。

paragraphs: PepsiCo 是一家全球領先的飲料與便利食品公司，擁有相互補充的品牌組合，包括 Lay's、Doritos、Cheetos、Gatorade、Pepsi-Cola、Mountain Dew、Quaker 和 SodaStream。透過我們的營運、授權灌裝商、合約製造商及其他第三方，我們製造、行銷、分銷與銷售廣泛的飲料與便利食品，服務超過 200 個國家與地區的客戶與消費者。

作為一家擁有強大本地連接的全球公司，我們在 2025 年面臨與全球消費者、客戶與競爭對手相同的許多挑戰。這些挑戰包括持續的供應鏈中斷；關稅；持續的通貨膨脹壓力；消費者的消費模式與偏好不斷變化；高度競爭的商業環境，包括人工智慧技術的採用增加；電商在快速變化的零售環境中持續擴張，包括消費者逐漸離開 DSD 系統；我們在朝向雄心勃勃的包裝及其他目標前進時，需要進一步的創新與合作；持續的總體經濟與政治不穩定；以及日益複雜的法規環境。
為回應這些挑戰，我們持續適應與創新，強化我們的韌性與持續專注於成長。我們致力於提升生產力，優化營運，並透過我們的市場運用規模與能力，進一步提高消費者在策略中的興趣、場合與通路，以領導並塑造我們類別的未來。這是以 pep+（PepsiCo Positive）轉型為基礎，目前已進入第五年。
明確願景：在這樣的背景下，我們有明確的優先事項：透過結合營運以達到最佳效益，重啟我們的北美業務，並利用節省下來的資源支持對品牌的有意義投資；增加國際業務的規模、存在感與規模，專注於在大型與發展中的市場中捕捉成長；並努力擴大我們的外食業務，透過擴大可見度並拓展至新的場合。
奠定基礎：自 2018 年以來，我們已對業務進行重大投資，以適應變化的環境。這包括增加投資以強化品牌，從透過創新與收購轉型品牌組合，到基礎建設資訊科技與人工智慧，以使我們具備未來的適應力，建立一套高影響力的商業、營運與數位能力；擴展與更新製造設施，以實現地理成長與捕捉未來需求；調整規模並現代化倉儲與分銷能力；並轉型營運模式，使其更具靈活性、效率與對消費者的回應力。

對重大事物進行重大改變：在 pep+ 的引導下，我們持續努力重塑我們的產品組合，以適應當前的環境。這包括：減少核心品牌如 Lay's 與 Gatorade 中的添加糖、鈉與飽和脂肪；推動去除人工色素與風味的進程，如 Lay's、Cheet、Doritos 等品牌；增加具有功能效益的新產品，例如 Pepsi Prebiotic Cola；並歡迎如 Siete、Sabra 與 poppi 等受歡迎的品牌。
我們持續擴展外食業務至新的場合。成功的 Walking Taco 平台在美國的體育場、體育館與公園中蓬勃發展，而我們的 "Food Deserves Pepsi" 行動與 "Pepsi Zero Sugar Taste Challenge" 行動已提高品牌知名度，並對我們的表現產生正面影響。

我們正在成為一個更深入整合、更高效的組織。這是我們過去一年最重要的優先事項。自我們在 2025 年初轉型營運模式後，我們努力變得更具靈活性、簡化與統一。從共享全球服務，到簡化流程，到推出近 25 年來的第一個新企業品牌識別，我們正在實現 One PepsiCo。在北美，我們正在仔細評估食品與飲料供應鏈、市場進入與商業能力的整合模式，並有意採用考慮投資回報率、規模與市場佔有率等關鍵要素的細膩方法。我們的全球能力中心現在支援多種功能，使我們能夠集中資訊、減少重複工作，並在組織內分享最佳實務。
我們正在利用人工智慧等技術建立更聰明的系統，以更好地服務客戶與消費者，使我們能擁有正確的產品，在正確的地點，以正確的價格。透過與尖端科技供應商的合作，我們正在利用人工智慧重新設計我們的市場推廣模式，提升客戶支援，並賦能銷售團隊專注於戰略性成長。這使我們能統一資料，取得即時的存貨可見性，並提供更快、更具回應性的客戶服務。
我們正在透過 pep+ 提升韌性。pep+ 備受我們策略的核心，確保我們持續為股東、客戶與消費者創造價值，同時為社區與地球做正確的事。2025 年，我們在再生農業與用水效率等關鍵支柱上加強了努力，目標是對全球市場產生正面影響。

paragraphs: 以下風險，有些已經發生，任何一種都可能在未來發生，可能對我們的業務或財務表現造成重大不利影響，進而影響我們公開交易證券的價格。這些並非我們所面臨的唯一風險。我們可能還面臨其他風險，目前尚未察覺，或目前認為不具重大性，但未來可能變得重要。

我們產品的需求部分取決於我們創新與預測並有效回應消費者趨勢與偏好的變動，包括消費者想要的產品類型，以及他們如何瀏覽、購買與消費這些產品。消費者偏好持續因多種因素而改變，包括：消費者人口結構的變化、消費模式（包括在外進食的食品增加）、飲食習慣（無論是因消費者行為與飲食習慣改變、使用減重藥物，如GLP-1藥物，或其他因素）以及通路偏好（包括電子商務與線上到線下通路持續增加，以及使用人工智慧購物代理人自主選擇產品，這些產品可能不屬於我們）；價格（包括因產品成分而對製造、分銷或銷售某些產品所課徵關稅與稅收的有效影響）；負擔壓力與消費支出模式的變化（包括消費者轉向自有品牌或較低價位的產品）；對我們產品包含在福利計畫中的資金支持或限制，例如美國的補助糧食計畫（Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program, SNAP）；產品品質；產品功能（包括高蛋白或富含纖維的產品）；對包裝及其環境影響的擔憂或觀感（例如一次性或其他塑膠包裝）；對加工過程、營養組成與健康影響，或成分或包裝來源地的擔憂或觀感，包括因政府官員的公開聲明、增加的訴訟、法規變更、監管審查或第三方研究結果（無論科學有效性如何）；以及對我們員工政策與倡議的擔憂或觀感。

疫情、流行病或其他疾病爆發，以及地緣政治事件與緊張關係、戰爭與其他軍事衝突也已影響並可能繼續影響消費者偏好與對我們產品的需求，包括對非本地產品的負面消費情緒。消費者偏好也受到我們品牌形象或產品品牌形象、我們廣告與行銷活動的成功、我們能否以消費者偏好的方式與消費者互動（包括使用數位媒體或資產），以及我們使用社交媒體與對政治與社會議題、地緣政治事件與緊張關係、戰爭與其他軍事衝突或災難性事件的回應的觀感影響。這些及其他因素已降低並可能繼續降低消費者購買我們某些產品的意願，包括因公開抵制所致。我們若無法預測或回應消費者偏好與趨勢的變化，或做出正確的戰略投資，包括投資人工智慧與數據分析以瞭解消費者趨勢，將導致產品需求減少，導致存貨減損或削弱我們的競爭與財務地位，進而對我們的業務造成不利影響。此外，我們的業務運作，包括供應鏈，可能因地緣政治事件與緊張關係、戰爭與其他軍事衝突、自然災害、疫情、流行病或其他我們無法控制的事件而受到幹擾。
我們的業務運作，包括供應鏈，可能因地緣政治事件與緊張關係、戰爭與其他軍事衝突、自然災害、疫情、流行病或其他我們無法控制的事件而受到幹擾，這些事件可能對產品供應造成負面影響，並降低對我們產品的需求，如果我們的危機管理計畫無法有效緩解這些問題的話。

維持全球正面的聲譽對我們的業務至關重要。我們的聲譽或品牌形象過去曾因多種因素而受到不利影響，未來也可能受到不利影響，包括：我們、我們的業務夥伴或其他供應鏈參與者未能維持高道德、商業與環境、社會及治理（ESG）實踐，包括與人權、童工、員工政策與倡議、工作環境與員工健康與安全相關的方面；未能達成或未能足夠進展我們的ESG目標，或對這些目標的任何修訂或負面看法，包括與我們產品的營養組成、包裝、用水、對環境的影響以及我們的員工政策與倡議相關的方面；執行我們戰略倡議的困難；未能解決對我們產品、我們分銷的產品、授權給第三方並分銷的特定品牌（包括酒精飲料）或我們產品中的特定成分或物質的健康或其他擔憂，包括對我們某些產品是否為「超加工食品」、是否含有特定成分或物質或是否導致肥胖及其他健康問題或增加公共衛生成本的擔憂；我們的研究與開發努力；任何產品品質或安全問題，包括召回我們的產品；未能遵守法律與法規；消費者對我們廣告活動、贊助安排、行銷計畫、使用社交媒體及我們對政治與社會議題、地緣政治事件與緊張關係、戰爭與其他軍事衝突或災難性事件的回應的觀感；或未能有效回應社交媒體或其他方面對我們的負面或不正確評論。我們聲譽或品牌形象的損害過去曾並可能未來導致對我們產品需求的減少，進而對我們的業務造成不利影響。

我們因產品品質或安全問題而召回，並可能在未來召回產品，包括實際或聲稱的標籤錯誤、品牌錯誤、變質、未申明的過敏原、污染或混入異物。我們參與的合資企業也因相同或其它原因而召回，並可能在未來召回產品。這些風險可能因新或演進的法規、我們產品組合的變化（包括增加功能性或其他成分的使用）、基礎設施老化，以及供應鏈中我們供應商的壓力增加而更加嚴重。產品召回過去曾並可能未來對我們的業務造成不利影響，導致因召回成本、產品存貨的毀損、消費者罰款與退貨或因產品短時間無法取得而導致的銷售減少。此外，我們的製造設施與產品已並可能繼續受到聯邦、州與地方政府機構的更嚴格檢查。我們或政府機構識別出的產品品質或安全問題過去曾並可能未來降低消費者對我們產品的信心與需求，導致生產與配送中斷，包括因製造廠或設施暫時或永久關閉所致，導致成本增加（包括支付罰款與/或判決金、清潔與整治成本與法律費用，以及替代生產來源的相關成本），並損害我們的聲譽（或我們參與的合資企業的聲譽），特別是當我們或我們的合資企業持續擴張至新產品類別時，所有這些都可能對我們的業務造成不利影響。任何對我們未能維持足夠產品品質或安全監督的觀感或指控（無論是否屬實）都可能導致產品召回、訴訟、政府調查、檢查或詢問，或民事或刑事程序，所有這些都可能導致罰款、處罰、賠償、刑事責任、聲譽損害或消費者需求的變化。我們的業務也可能因消費者對產品失去信心而受到不利影響
